hypothesis: The three residual taxi violations can be repaired by adding a small, symmetry-aware linear functional of the normalized work function to the verified n=5 prior-art potential, while preserving every complete-circle inequality.
rationale: The residual failures are three taxi-only zero-distance transitions with base slack -1, whereas the complete-circle control has 4710 tight inequalities. A constrained additive correction is a structurally different potential mechanism from coefficient perturbation: it directly asks whether the residual edge directions lie outside the cone imposed by the complete-circle constraints. Grouping features by pairwise circular-distance signature keeps the correction permutation- and rotation-invariant and gives a portable rule for m=8 rather than an arbitrary per-coordinate lookup.
expected_information_gain: Determines whether a low-dimensional symmetry-aware correction cone can repair the residual mechanism at all. Feasibility would produce a candidate for full taxi evaluation and generalization; infeasibility or taxi regression would close this targeted correction family without broad coefficient tuning.
method: Use the fixed published n=5 index matrix and coefficients as the base. Define 16 features by summing normalized work-function entries over configuration classes with each of the pairwise circular-distance signatures present at m=6. Solve four bounded L1 linear programs: require all 6006 complete-circle inequalities to remain nonnegative and require correction slack on all three residual taxi edges, then on each of the three residual pairs. Bounds are -10 to 10 per feature weight; select no model using taxi results before solving. Evaluate every feasible correction on all 7,000,602 taxi inequalities; only a count below 3 earns primary-evaluator confirmation.
metric: complete-circle violations_k and frozen circle-taxi violations_k; target is taxi violations_k < 3
metric_relation_to_true_objective: The complete-circle constraints and residual-edge constraints are finite gates. Only the full frozen taxi count below 3 is strict finite objective improvement; even zero finite violations is not a proof of the full k-server conjecture.

configuration.feature_signature: sorted six pairwise circular distances of each 4-server multiset configuration
configuration.generalization_rule: feature weights apply to matching pairwise-distance signatures; unmatched m=8 signatures receive zero correction

compute_budget.cpu: WSL2 pinned metric arrays; four LP models and conditional full taxi counts
compute_budget.memory_intent: low-dimensional LP followed by bounded finite evaluation; no evaluator changes

kill_condition: Stop after the four declared LP models, at 1800 seconds, or at a precise runtime failure. Do not add features, loosen bounds, or fit new constraints after seeing results. If no feasible model exists, close this correction family. If feasible models exist, evaluate only those declared models on the full taxi metric and primary-evaluate only a strict target result.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: a full taxi count below 3 is required for strict improvement

previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: the correction is a new mechanism layered on the verified baseline

interpretation: Pending constrained solve and full finite evaluation; no correction candidate is yet claimed.
what_was_learned: Pending execution; the experiment tests whether residual-edge repair is possible in a symmetry-aware low-dimensional correction cone.
recommended_next_action: Evaluate every feasible correction across the complete taxi metric; if none reaches fewer than 3, close this correction family and pause k-server.
repetition_justification: This is not a coefficient perturbation or min-envelope parameter sweep. It introduces an additive, symmetry-aware work-function feature correction constrained specifically by the residual edge geometry.
